usage: Treatment of susceptible bacterial infections including specified infections of the ear/nose/throat, genitourinary tract, skin/skin structure, and lower respiratory tract; certain adult regimens also use it with other medicines for H. pylori-associated duodenal ulcer disease. Indication depends on susceptible organisms and product label.
symptoms: Exact adverse-reaction frequencies vary by product label. The current label includes warnings for serious hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis and drug-induced enterocolitis syndrome; reported reactions can include gastrointestinal upset and rash. Do not infer a frequency from another formulation without checking its label.

usage: Treatment of susceptible bacterial infections including selected sinus, ear, lower respiratory, skin/soft-tissue, and urinary tract infections; the exact approved indications depend on formulation and label.
symptoms: Common label-reported adverse reactions: diarrhea/loose stools (about 9%), nausea (about 3%), skin rash/urticaria (about 3%), vomiting (about 1%), and vaginitis (about 1%). Important serious label warnings include anaphylaxis/severe hypersensitivity, severe skin reactions, liver dysfunction, drug-induced enterocolitis syndrome, and C. difficile-associated diarrhea.

usage: Treatment of susceptible bacterial infections including selected respiratory tract, otitis media, skin/skin-structure, bone, and genitourinary infections, as specified in the product label.
symptoms: Use the exact product label for adverse-reaction frequencies and serious warnings; do not infer a drug-specific adverse-effect list from the cephalosporin class. The FDA label source identified here confirms indications but this entry remains incomplete for adverse-reaction extraction.

usage: Treatment of specified susceptible bacterial infections; indications vary by age, formulation, organism, and label. Use only for a diagnosed or strongly suspected bacterial infection when appropriate.
symptoms: Common label-reported adverse reactions include diarrhea (about 5% or 5–14% depending on regimen/label), nausea (about 3%), abdominal pain (about 3%), and vomiting. Important serious label warnings include hypersensitivity, liver injury, QT prolongation/arrhythmia, C. difficile-associated diarrhea, infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis, and worsening myasthenia gravis.

usage: Treatment of specific infections caused by susceptible bacteria, including certain urinary, gastrointestinal, skin, bone/joint, and other infections; indications are restricted by label for some uncomplicated conditions because of serious adverse effects.
symptoms: FDA/DailyMed boxed warning: tendinitis and tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, central nervous system effects, and worsening myasthenia gravis; some effects can be disabling and potentially irreversible. Common reactions depend on formulation and indication; check the linked product label for the exact adverse-reaction table.

usage: Treatment of specified infections caused by susceptible organisms; also has selected non-antibacterial indications depending on product/label. Exact use depends on formulation and diagnosis.
symptoms: Label-reported reactions include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, appetite loss, rash, photosensitivity (exaggerated sunburn), and urticaria. Warnings include C. difficile-associated diarrhea; esophagitis/esophageal ulceration has been reported with oral tablets/capsules; tetracyclines during tooth development can cause permanent tooth discoloration/enamel effects.

usage: Treatment of serious infections caused by susceptible bacteria; product labels include injection use and require clinical monitoring. Exact indications depend on formulation and local label.
symptoms: The label carries a boxed warning for potentially nephrotoxic (kidney-damaging) and ototoxic (hearing/balance-damaging) effects, with greater nephrotoxicity risk in impaired renal function and with high-dose/prolonged treatment. Monitor for reduced urine output, hearing changes, ringing in the ears, dizziness/vertigo, and balance problems; the label should be checked for route-specific reactions.

usage: Treatment of specified serious infections caused by susceptible anaerobic bacteria and susceptible gram-positive organisms; exact indications depend on route and product label.
symptoms: Label-reported adverse reactions include abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, itching, and liver-test abnormalities. Important serious risk: C. difficile-associated diarrhea/colitis, which can occur during or after treatment; severe skin reactions and anaphylactic reactions have also been reported.

usage: Treatment of susceptible urinary tract infections; product/formulation and renal function affect suitability. It is not a general-purpose antibiotic for infections outside its indicated urinary tract use.
symptoms: Label-reported adverse reactions include nausea (about 8%), headache (about 6%), and flatulence (about 1.5%); also reported are diarrhea, dyspepsia, abdominal pain, constipation, vomiting, dizziness, drowsiness, rash/urticaria, fever, chills, and malaise. Serious pulmonary hypersensitivity and other pulmonary reactions are described in warnings.
